subject: Dedicated Capacity intake — QuantumAI concurrency & token profile
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rao <aisha@quantum.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated Capacity intake — QuantumAI concurrency & token profile

Hi Aisha,

Good to meet you last week — thanks again for the demo. To get the Dedicated sizing right (and to produce a realistic cost/latency plan for the pilot), can you fill out the attached intake? I attached our lightweight dedicated-sizer spreadsheet; if it's easier, paste answers into the body.

High-level asks we need to understand:
- Peak QPS and sustained QPS windows (please specify local timezone).
- Prompt/response token distributions (median, p90, p99 for both).
- Percent of traffic that is chat-style multi-turn with KV cache hits vs stateless single-shot calls.
- Ratio of heavy-long-context ops (document summarization/search with >8k tokens) vs short completions.
- Percentage of requests that include an embeddings/reranker pipeline before generation.
- Any strict p99 latency SLOs and acceptable fallbacks (e.g. fallback to smaller model at higher P99).

Notes for the intake: we usually recommend providing a 7-day telemetry extract if possible (we can accept a sample CSV). If you have a preferred GPU SKU (A100/RTX etc) or hard requirements (on-prem, VPC-only), please flag that.

Next steps: if you return the completed sheet + a short telemetry sample, Marissa will run the sizing model and we’ll schedule a 45-min session to review the results and options (pilot vs reserved).

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizer-template.xlsx

Thanks —
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Pre-sales, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.ai

From: Aisha Rao <aisha@quantum.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@quantum.ai
Date: 2028-10-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated Capacity intake — QuantumAI concurrency & token profile

Thanks Vivek — attaching a short telemetry extract and a partially filled sheet. High level details below (happy to fill anything missing).

Quick answers:
- Peak QPS: 120 qps during US business hours (14:00–15:30 UTC), sustained 40 qps the rest of the day. We see brief micro-bursts to ~220 qps for <10 minutes when campaigns run.
- Prompt tokens: median prompt 75 tokens, p90 420, p99 2,100. Response tokens: median 80, p90 1,200, p99 6,000 (summaries).
- Multi-turn chat: ~38% of requests are multi-turn; KV cache hit estimated at 65% (we use session-affinity for active sessions).
- Long-context ops: ~6% of requests involve >8k tokens (document summarization/search across multi-docs).
- Embeddings/reranker: approx 27% of sessions call embeddings then run a re-ranker before generation (pipeline latency budget ~120ms).
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 300ms for short completions; for long-context ops we target p95 <= 2s. For p99 we are tolerant of higher latency but aim for <5s.
- Preferred GPU: we have an internal preference for NVIDIA H100s (we own a private cluster but want Redwood Dedicated for burst and SLA).

Attaching: qai-telemetry-sample.csv and the partially completed redwood-dedicated-sizer-template.xlsx. Let me know if you want more days.

Regards,
Aisha Rao
Head of Product, QuantumAI
aisha@quantum.ai

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rao <aisha@quantum.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-20T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated Capacity intake — QuantumAI concurrency & token profile

Aisha — this is great, thanks for the sample. A few clarifying points before Marissa runs the sizing:

1) Bursts: when you say micro-bursts to ~220 qps for <10 minutes, are those concurrent unique sessions or repeated requests from the same sessions? That affects KV cache / batching assumptions.

2) Long-context ops: the 6% >8k tokens — are those typically multi-turn dialogs that continue after the summarization (i.e., do they re-open the KV cache), or are they one-off summary jobs?

3) Embeddings pipeline: is the reranker synchronous in-path for user requests or async (we need to know if it increases tail latency and whether it can be batched independently).

4) Can procurement@quantum.ai be looped into the pilot contract conversation? We'll need an acknowledgement on pilot duration and expected reserved commitment if the pilot looks good.

Marissa — marking for sizing run. Key knobs we will include:
- Model mix: mixture of 13B chat for short completions, 70B quantized for summarization, and a smaller 2.7B reranker for embeddings pipeline.
- Batching policy: continuous batching for short completions with a 30ms batching window when under 80 qps; burst pre-warm for known campaign windows.
- KV cache sizing: assume 65% hit-rate initially; we will model both 65% and 80% scenarios.

Proposed next steps: Marissa to produce a capacity plan + cost delta for a 4-week pilot (burst enabled) vs a 3-month reserved commitment. Can you confirm a good time for the review session next week (I can do Wed/Thu mornings PST)?

Thanks —
Vivek

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-22T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: QuantumAI pricing & pilot note

Internal note (cc'd to thread for context):

I ran a quick back-of-envelope using Aisha's telemetry: projected steady-state for her 40 qps baseline with the token mix is ~18 A100-equivalent GPUs if we assume conservative per-GPU throughput for 70B quantized summarization workloads. If we assume H100s and apply our quantization optimizations, that drops to ~12 H100-equivalents.

Pilot recommendation: start with a 6-week pilot with a 2-week pre-warm and a 4-week live burst window that covers campaign dates. Contract terms to propose:
- Pilot: fixed monthly pilot fee covering reserved baseline capacity (12 H100-eq) + burst credit pool for up to 200 qps for 2 x 10-minute bursts per day.
- If pilot converts within 30 days of completion, move to a 12-month Reserved plan with gradual up-commit if observed KV hit-rate stays >=70%.

Marissa — can you turn this into a short slide and a pilot quote? Vivek, Aisha — I’ll wait for your go/no-go on the Wed/Thu review window.

Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
